subject: general
question: In May 2022, the Supreme Court has restrained the state and central governments from invoking which charges, under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code, against anybody?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Sedition__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **state and federal governments** **are not allowed to accuse anyone of sedition invoking Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code, according to the Supreme Court.**
 
• Until the Center analyses the statute from the British era, the order will be in effect.
 
• It stated that until the law is reviewed, no new** FIRs **will be filed, investigations won't be conducted, and no further coercive actions under sedition will be performed.
 
• It is a** cognizable, non-bailable, non-compoundable offence.**
 
• It can be punished by imprisonment of three years or a fine or both.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inchoate**

 
 
• **​Inchoate crimes are actions taken that are intended to be criminal acts or that amount to indirect participation in illegal acts.**
 
• Although such a deed might not be a criminal in and of itself, it is done to further or advance a crime.
 
 
 
• **Bankruptcy**
 
 
• ​Through the **legal process of bankruptcy**,** individuals or other entities that cannot pay their creditors back can seek partial or complete relief from their debts.**
 
• **Bankruptcy** is typically imposed by a court order frequently requested by the debtor.
 
• A person who is **insolvent** may have more than **one legal status;** consequently, the term "**bankruptcy**" **is not a synonym for insolvency.**
 
 
 
• **Homicide**
 
 
• **​When someone kills another person, it is called homicide**.
 
• A homicide merely needs to be a **voluntary action or omission** that results in the death of another person; therefore, it can result from** careless, irresponsible, or accidental behaviour** even when no malice was intended.
